What it is

One small stylesheet (15 KB, 11 KB minified, zero dependencies, no build step) that gives a page finished defaults, a themable token system, a handful of layout primitives and a few opt-in components. It is the styling half of Colibri: Colibri UI provides headless behaviour, Colibri CSS provides the look.

Why we built it

We wanted pages that look right with plain, semantic HTML, the kind FreeMarker templates and CMS content produce, without picking between two bad options:

Utility frameworks
Every element gets twenty classes, you need a compiler, and the design is spread across thousands of lines of markup. Changing the design means editing templates.
Heavy frameworks
Hundreds of KB, specificity fights, and a site that looks like the framework instead of your product.

Modern CSS now does natively what those tools were invented to work around. Colibri CSS is a thin, opinionated layer over the platform.

How it works

Cascade layers

Everything sits in @layer colibri.*. Your own CSS outside a layer always wins: no !important, no specificity wars.

Design tokens

Colour, space, type, radius, shadow and motion are custom properties. OKLCH colours come from one --c-hue, so one number re-brands everything.

Dark mode built in

Every colour is a light-dark() pair. Follows the OS; data-theme forces it on any element.

Fluid type & space

clamp() scales grow smoothly from phone to desktop, with no breakpoints to maintain.

Layout primitives

.stack .cluster .grid .split .switcher .center .reel .prose, tuned with --gap, --min and --side instead of new classes.

Container queries

Cards respond to the space they're in, so one piece of markup fits a sidebar and a main column.

:has() patterns

Selected cards, invalid-field labels and required markers, with no JavaScript.

Native nesting

States and variants live in one readable block. Variants are attributes: data-variant, data-size, data-tone.

Accessible defaults

Keyboard focus rings, reduced-motion tokens, high-contrast borders, slim scrollbars and tinted native controls.

Bridge to Colibri UI

colibri-ui-bridge.css maps --ui-* to --c-*: headless components and your page share one palette and one dark mode.
